audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) Three strings credit Olaf's W with the sustain — 'W-sustain', 'W-omnivamp', 'your W heals through her autos'. Riot's text for the W is only 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield'; the lifesteal is the passive, Berserker Rage, and it scales with MISSING health. (b) Divine Judgment's 160/120/80s cooldown is never stated anywhere, and the kit's derived flag calls it 'untargetable' while Riot's own description says 'makes an ally invulnerable'.
audit.why: (a) reverses how Olaf survives an extended trade: the shield is a one-shot buffer, the lifesteal gets STRONGER as he drops, which is exactly why you commit low rather than back off. (b) 160s at rank 1 is the longest cooldown in the lane and the whole level-6 window hangs on baiting it. Invulnerable, not untargetable, matters concretely: Reckless Swing still targets her, deals zero, and still costs Olaf the health with no refund because he did not destroy the target.
audit.corrected: Berserker Rage and Tough It Out named in spikes[1].text, whys[4] and wants.you[1]. The 160s rank-1 cooldown written into dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why. dontsFull[1].d now states the E-into-invulnerability health loss. Per instructions I trusted Riot's description over the misfiring 'untargetable' flag and wrote invulnerable.

notes: Two systemic issues visible from this page. (1) Olaf's sustain is attributed to his W across the whole repo's Olaf pages; it belongs to the passive Berserker Rage and scales with missing health. The mirror agent on kassadin found the same thing and also found the W being called by its pre-rework name 'Vicious Strikes' — this page uses the generic 'W-sustain' in tradeGood, breakdown.trading and report[3].t, which is not wrong enough to rewrite three long strings but is worth a bulk pass. (2) The kit file's derived flag for Divine Judgment says 'untargetable'; Riot's description says 'invulnerable'. I wrote invulnerable per the standing rule. Kayle is female and dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, tradeGood and report[12].t all call her 'he'/'his' — pronoun-only, not fixed here. Chart flipped in matched pairs to the packet/mirror order.
